nodes.text:
Server resource and draft API
UI calls resource list/create/get/remove/reset plus draft get/patch/commit/discard/reload operations.

Renderer boundary
`ArchitectureIsland` lazily bridges Solid to React/React Flow; desktop resolves renderer dependencies and `direction`/`mobile` props drive responsive placement while the canvas stays LTR.

Graph panel controller
Loads and switches resources, persists selection and viewport, journals drafts, reconciles events and conflicts, and coordinates Save, reload, and resource deletion.

AI context integration
Resource mentions identify managed Graph context; selected nodes can be sent as follow-up prompt context.

Implemented audit: Save/Reload state ownership map
Mapped the current visible Graph state writers: query cache, persisted drafts/viewports, live draft synchronizer, event handlers, local Save/Reload operations, React editor history, React Flow nodes/edges, dirty state, resource list, reload generation, and tab lifecycle. The key remaining failure path was local Save/Reload success racing with draft updated/discarded events that could cancel synchronizer cleanup or keep saved-covered live drafts dirty.

Architecture capability
`useServerArchitectureAvailable` probes the authenticated architecture route and gates Graph visibility in session UI.

Implemented improvement: colored remote-edit glow
Agent/external node changes use a dedicated theme-aware amber hint color for the border, glow, and background tint; the effect remains transient and clears on pointer movement.

Implemented feature: duplicate graph
A duplicate action clones the current saved/live graph state into a new managed resource, preserving nodes, edges, tags, colors, connection sides/styles, and positions; the original remains unchanged and the duplicate becomes selected.

Implemented feature: export graph
Exports the current visible graph state, including unsaved draft changes, as a portable `<name>.graph.json` file without mutating the resource, draft, selection, or viewport.

Implemented improvement: resource File menu
New graph, Duplicate graph, and Delete graph now live in a File dropdown beside the selector; switching remains explicit and existing confirmations/action behavior are preserved. Export remains a separate editor action.

Implemented fix: remote edit hint
When an agent or external resource sync creates, changes, or moves a node, show a subtle temporary color or glow until the user's pointer moves over it. Local edits, drags, undo, and redo do not add the hint; the state stays out of Graph context.

Planned fix: multi-select deletion
Node context-menu Delete should remove every currently selected node, not only the node that opened the menu; preserve selection cleanup and undo behavior.

Implemented fix: remove editor action bar
The top action bar is gone and right-click menus are unchanged. Standard shortcuts: Ctrl+Z undo, Ctrl+Shift+Z redo, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+R reload. Add node, Fit view, Delete, and export remain available through the command infrastructure and context actions.

Implemented fix: stable resource selector
Hovering or highlighting another resource does not switch the graph. Explicit selection is committed through the controlled selector; persisted readiness and stale-list reconciliation keep the chosen graph displayed instead of snapping back to the first one.

Implemented fix: local Save/Reload transaction guard
During local Save or Reload, draft updated/discarded events are captured instead of being allowed to invalidate or overwrite the in-flight authoritative transition. Successful Save/Reload now always writes the returned saved snapshot, reconciles or clears live draft cache, clears persisted draft/journal state, updates resource summaries, advances renderer generation, and treats synchronizer cancellation after success as benign. Clean Save skips patch/commit work.

Implemented improvement: clean Ask about selection messages
Ask submissions now keep the user’s short question in the visible message and store the complete selected-node Graph brief as durable model-only context. Current and legacy provider paths receive the context exactly once; rendering, copy, prompt restoration, retry, revert, queued followups, resend, and accessibility expose only the visible question. The Ask textarea has an accessible name and a compact context-attached indicator.

Implemented tactical fix, but user testing still reports buggy Save/Reload
This pass added draft serialization, cache generation guards, discard re-observation, and mounted Reload reset. It reduced known races but did not establish one authoritative editor state owner: the unsaved hint can still remain after Save, Reload can appear visually stale until tab remount, and UI state still crosses query cache, persisted journal, synchronizer queue, and React/React Flow local state. Supersede with the state-authority redesign rather than adding more isolated guards.

React Flow editor
Edits text nodes, free-form tags and colors, explicit four-side connections, filters, selection/inspector, undo/redo, export, and edge routing.

Planned/partially implemented redesign: authoritative Graph editor state controller
Completed a targeted transaction-guard step: local Save/Reload now capture their own draft events, apply authoritative server results unconditionally, centralize visible dirty-state derivation, skip clean Save work, and force renderer generation forward after clean transitions. Broader direction remains: collapse query cache, persisted journal, synchronizer queue, React editor history, and React Flow projection into one explicit per-resource controller if manual testing still finds stale UI.

Session navigation
Desktop opens Graph in the special side-panel tab; mobile exposes a full-content Architecture tab and hides the composer while it is active.

Test plan: Graph draft/Save consistency
1. Apply an AI draft update and delay the draft fetch. 2. Make a local edit and invoke Save. 3. Resolve the delayed fetch after commit. Assert the canvas and cache remain on the committed snapshot and the live draft stays empty. Repeat with an AI edit during synchronization/commit, Reload, and resource switching; assert no stale graph returns and no operations are lost or duplicated. Verify event payloads under both properties and data.
